summary: Drum & bass (liquid first): 170-176 BPM two-step on chopped breaks, a deep sub or growling reese in long half-time notes, minor 7th/9th chords on Rhodes, piano or lush pads, a soft melodic line; knowledge/style/dnb.json is its template
body: Tempo 170-180 BPM, most tracks at 174; felt at half speed (85-87).

Drums: the two-step (kick on 1 and the and of 3, snares on 2 and 4) from one-shots, with a pitched-up classic break (Think, Amen) layered as a high-passed top loop; 8th hats, a 16th shaker, ghost snares 6-12 dB down around the backbeats, a ghost kick before the bar line.

Bass: the sub is the foundation, low (around F0-F1), in long notes that follow the drums, a variation every other four bars and a two-beat gap at the end of 16 for the turnaround; a reese (detuned saws) or a growling mid bass on top in rollers and neuro.
Harmony: liquid uses lush minor 7th and 9th chords (i-VII-VI is the common loop) on Rhodes, soulful piano (often low-passed) and wide pads, held through the bar; jump-up and neuro have almost none.
Lead: a soft melody: piano, a vocal chop, bells or (the producer's rule, 2026-11-26) a soothing vibraphone an octave lower than a bright lead would sit.
Texture/master: clean, punchy and loud; crisp snares, a mono sub, reverb sends tying the pads together; a transparent limiter, no lofi roll-off or saturation.
Sources (2026-11-26): EDMProd 'How to make liquid drum and bass' and 'How to make drum and bass'; Native Instruments 'Drum and bass'; MusicRadar 'How to create a throbbing Reese-style sub-bass'.
Apply: pattern/dnb-two-step on the drums, then pattern/prog-drum-and-bass-common-1 on the keys four bars later. For a whole style change the Team Lead's restyle uses knowledge/style/dnb.json instead.

drums.about: the drum track (a kit); leave out if there isn't one

keys.about: a chordal part (keys, pad); leave out if there isn't one

key.about: the project's key; leave out to estimate it from the notes
